findings.title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises if default_locale is nil
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the site setting before compacting. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil (e.g. during early boot, before site settings are provisioned, or a blank setting), this raises NoMethodError inside every I18n lookup's fallback resolution, breaking all translation. The `.compact` is also ineffective for this case since the exception happens earlier. Guard with `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores fallback chain / default locale
findings.body: With fallbacks enabled, the result of `translate(key)` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of the fallback chain), but the LRU cache key is only `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. In multisite (or after an admin changes the default locale) the same process can serve sites with different default locales, so a cached value resolved via site A's fallback locale will be returned for site B, producing wrong-language strings. Include the fallback chain (or default_locale) in the cache key, or clear the cache when default_locale changes.

findings.title: Fallback locales only loaded in web requests
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Because the translate_accelerator only lazily loads the yml for `config.locale`, any code path outside controllers (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) that sets a locale will never load the fallback locale files, so fallback lookups return 'translation missing' instead of the default-locale/English string. The ensure_loaded! call should happen wherever the locale is set (e.g. in I18n.locale= or in the backend/translate path).

findings.title: ensure_loaded! initializes @loaded_locales outside the mutex
findings.body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` and the `include?` check run outside LOAD_MUTEX, while load_locale mutates `@loaded_locales` under the mutex. Concurrent requests can race, re-initializing the array to [] and discarding already-loaded locale bookkeeping (triggering redundant reloads) or reading a partially-updated array. Move initialization/check inside the mutex (or initialize eagerly at load time).
